note: The evaluation grid the verifier schedules, and the telemetry the locked loop writes at every point on it. instruction.md defines the graded quantity in words; this file is where the loop reads the grid from, so the cadence, the last scheduled point and the two readout channels are properties of the run rather than numbers you are asked to guess. train_baseline.py loads this file and refuses to run a schedule that disagrees with it.

evaluation_grid.note: The verifier evaluates at first_eval_step and every evaluation_cadence_steps thereafter, up to and including last_scheduled_step. There is no scheduled point after last_scheduled_step, so a crossing whose sustain window would close past it cannot be observed at all.

halt_rule.meaning: The optimizer step at which the run stopped, written into run.halt_step of the telemetry record. The loop halts on schedule exhaustion, which is last_scheduled_step, unless it is stopped earlier.
halt_rule.early_stop_is_not_a_crossing: A run whose halt_step lands before the sustain window of the first favourable evaluation has closed is graded as not having crossed, with the reason run-halted-before-sustain-window-closed. Halting early does not record an absent result; it records a zero.

verifier_raw_loss.meaning: The unsmoothed validation loss the harness computes at a scheduled point on the held-out split, written per evaluation row of the telemetry record. This is the only channel the graded quantity is read from.

submission_reported_loss.meaning: Your own reported loss, carried beside the graded channel for your diagnostics. It is never read on the graded path, and a submission that routes this channel into the graded one scores zero with readout-smoothed-on-the-graded-path.
